correctness.rationale: Counting crossing edges E(D,U) from the dominating outside vertices and the ≤1 outside neighbor per inside vertex gives |D|≥n, with equality iff every vertex has one crossing neighbor. Binary coloring crossing a_i=c_i XOR c_(i+1), b_i=c_i XOR c_(i+n) yields a_(i-1)+a_i+b_i=1. Subtract antipodal equations to obtain d_i=a_(i+n)−a_i=(-1)^i d_0, and chord parity b_i≡sum_(j=i)^(i+n-1) a_j (mod2); the even-n case forces alternating a_i, b_i=0 and n divisible4; odd n has no coherent case. For multiples of four there are two alternating a phases times global color complement, exactly four D and two cuts. For all other n the arc D={0,...,n} has n+1 vertices and satisfies both requirements. Independently brute-enumerated every subset for n=3..8 and reproduced equality multiplicity.
residual_risks: Brute force covers only n≤8; the binary crossing recurrence and parity argument are needed for the all-n result.
No count of n+1-optimal sets when 4∤n.
